correctness.rationale: Over C and odd m=2d+1≥5, the quadratic-outer composition map is a polynomial graph over coefficients of degrees m,...,2m−2 because the expansion H²+bH recovers the m−2 inner coefficients recursively and then b. Substitution t→−t induces parity involutions on the graph, so the graph map preserves even-coordinate fixed points. Subtracting its low-coefficient polynomial graph via an ambient triangular automorphism simultaneously makes the quadratic-outer and even-polynomial components linear. Their ideal intersection is (w_i,u_iv_j), giving the claimed ring, smooth intersection plane, normalization fiber product and conductor (u,v). Monomial counting proves the Hilbert–Samuel series. The exact sequence of the two smooth branches over their intersection gives depth d+1 and dimension 2d, proving non–Cohen–Macaulay for d≥2. The prime case follows from the checked Fried/Piene–Shapiro criterion. The standalone checker performed exact coefficient-reconstruction, tangent and finite Hilbert tests and passed; infinite claims follow from algebraic proof, not empirical tests.

value.rationale: Decomposability and invariant Bezoutian reducibility are natural algebraic-geometric parameter loci. A global polynomial straightening of two nonlinearly embedded composition components is structural, not an arbitrary finite slice. It yields their complete normalization-gluing conductor and all local Hilbert coefficients, and identifies a sharp, persistent non-Cohen–Macaulay boundary for the full prime-index reducibility locus despite its smooth components and smooth set-theoretic intersection. This qualitative homological change can affect intersection-theoretic and deformation analyses of composition strata; no unproved downstream application is asserted.
